newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Turns lower, cash market volatile.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Turns lower, cash market volatile.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices weakened on Friday, tracking a fall in swaps levels despite crude gains, traders said on Friday.
Late Friday, a 20,000-tonne cargo of 180-cst was traded at $97.50. The cargo, loading February 15-19, was sold by a firm based in Singapore to a Chinese trader, traders said.
Traders said the market fundamentals remained soft with supplies adequate to meet demand.
"Ample supplies were stored up in tanks in Singapore, resulting in the build in stocks in the Singapore statistics released yesterday," said a trader.
Residues stocks in Singapore were up by 820,000 barrels at 10.914 million barrels, according to the figures from the Trade Development Board released on Thursday.
Talk was also fairly thin with some traders expressing frustration at the cash price volatility.
"The market gained a dollar yesterday and fell a dollar today, making it quite hard to move any cargoes," said one trader.
The swaps market saw active trade with up to six deals heard done. A local trader was selling February paper to hedge earlier cash deals.
In the LSWR market, bid and offers were far apart and talk was thin. A bid was seen at $18.75 against offers at $21 for February supplies.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
